caveats: IMO's website (imo.net) was offline on build date due to a cyberattack; IMO 2027 shower data was confirmed via an indexed copy of the official 2027 calendar PDF plus timeanddate and Astronomy Now cross-checks.

No dates were invented: every event date comes from a cited source. Where reputable sources disagreed on the Mars–Jupiter conjunction date (Nov 15 vs Nov 16, 2026), the discrepancy is recorded in the entry.
Bortle classes are rough estimates from light-pollution maps, not on-site measurements; treat as planning guides.
Drive times are typical ranges from Medford/Boston and vary with traffic.
2027 lunar-phase notes in showers.json are derived from the IMO 2027 calendar's phase table (new/full moons), not from a dedicated ephemeris lookup.
The comet list is intentionally short: only 2P/Encke reaches credible naked-eye brightness in 2027, and even it peaks ~10° from the Sun. No faint comets were padded in.
Dark-sky site access rules change; confirm hours/fees before visiting. K.D. Dubuque is sunrise–sunset with night access via wilderness camping only; Cape Cod National Seashore closes at midnight.
Meteor shower dates for late 2027 are standard annual peaks; the app should re-verify against the IMO 2028 calendar when published.

coverage.comets.json: 2026-09-16 through 2027 — only credible mag ~6 or brighter prospects (1 found)
coverage.darksky.json: 59 DarkSky-certified dark-sky places across the U.S. (6 New England originals + 53 nationwide additions, 2026-09-16)
coverage.eclipses.json: every solar (14) and lunar (15) eclipse, 2026-09-16 through 2032-12, with New England visibility flags
coverage.showers.json: late-2026 peaks (6), all named major 2027 showers (11), notable minor showers (4)

project: Stargazer — verified sky-event datasets (data only, no app)
schema_note: Each file is an object with _source (array of source strings), an events/sites/solar/lunar array, and optional _note. This differs from the earlier array-only sketches; update the app's loader accordingly.
